basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 26.' and it opens 'Vers. 26. Sed et Seth natus est filius quem vocavit Enos. Enos homo interpretatur. Iste'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 26. Sed et Seth natus est filius quem vocavit Enos. Enos homo interpretatur. Iste coepit invocare | nomen Domini, id est colere Deum et deprecari, quamvis alia sit Hebraeorum opinio. Dicunt enim idola tunc primum facta et tanquam Deum adorata.
